source_text:
Ταπεινοφρονούντων γάρ ἐστιν ὁ Χριστός, οὐκ ἐπαιρομένων ἐπὶ τὸ ποίμνιον αὐτοῦ.
τὸ σκῆπτρον τῆς μεγαλωσύνης τοῦ θεοῦ, ὁ κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὐκ ἦλθεν ἐν κόμπῳ ἀλαζονείας οὐδὲ ὑπερηφανίας, καίπερ δυνάμενος, ἀλλὰ ταπεινοφρονῶν, καθὼς τὸ πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον περὶ αὐτοῦ ἐλάλησεν: φησὶν γάρ:
Κύριε. τίς ἐπίστευσεν τῇ ἀκοῇ ἡμῶν; καὶ ὁ βραχίων κυρίου τίνι ἀπεκαλύφθη; ἀνηγγείλαμεν ἐναντίον αὐτοῦ, ὡς παιδίον, ὡς ῥίζα ἐν γῇ διψώσῃ: οὐκ ἔστιν αὐτῷ εἶδος οὐδὲ δόξα, καὶ εἴδομεν αὐτόν, καὶ οὐκ εἶχεν εἶδος οὐδὲ κάλλος, ἀλλὰ τὸ εἶδος αὐτοῦ ἄτιμον, ἐκλεῖπον παρὰ τὸ εἶδος τῶν ἀνθρώπων: ἄνθρωπος ἐν πληγῇ ὢν καὶ πόνῳ καὶ εἰδὼς φέρειν μαλακίαν, ὅτι ἀπέστραπται τὸ πρόσωπον αὐτοῦ, ἠτιμάσθη καὶ οὐκ ἐλογίσθη:
οὗτος τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν φέρει καὶ περὶ ἡμῶν ὀδυνᾶται, καὶ ἡμεῖς ἐλογισάμεθα αὐτὸν εἶναι ἐν πόνῳ καὶ ἐν πληγῇ καὶ ἐν κακώσει:
αὐτὸς δὲ ἐτραυματίσθη διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας ἡμῶν καὶ μεμαλάκισται διὰ τὰς ἀνομίας ἡμῶν. παιδεία εἰρήνης ἡμῶν ἐπ’ αὐτόν: τῷ μώλωπι αὐτοῦ ἡμεῖς ἰάθημεν.
πάντες ὡς πρόβατα ἐπλανήθημεν, ἄνθρωπος τῇ ὁδῷ αὐτοῦ ἐπλανήθη:
καὶ κύριος παρέδωκεν αὐτὸν ὑπὲρ τῶν ἁμαρτιῶν ἡμῶν, καὶ αὐτὸς διὰ τὸ κεκακῶσθαι οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα. ὡς πρόβατον ἐπὶ σφαγὴν ἤχθη, καὶ ὡς ἀμνὸς ἐναντίον τοῦ κείραντος ἄφωνος, οὕτως οὐκ ἀνοίγει τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ. ἐν τῇ ταπεινώσει ἡ κρίσις αὐτοῦ ἤρθη.
τὴν γενεὰν αὐτοῦ τίς διηγήσεται; ὅτι αἴρεται ἀπὸ τῆς γῆς ἡ ζωὴ αὐτοῦ.
ἀπὸ τῶν ἀνομιῶν τοῦ λαοῦ μου ἥκει εἰς θάνατον.
καὶ δώσω τοὺς πονηροὺς ἀντὶ τῆς ταφῆς αὐτοῦ καὶ τοὺς πλουσίους ἀντὶ τοῦ θανάτου αὐτοῦ: ὅτι ἀνομίαν οὐκ ἐποίησεν, οὐδὲ εὑρέθη δόλος ἐν τῷ στόματι αὐτοῦ. καὶ κύριος βούλεται καθαρίσαι αὐτὸν τῆς πληγῆς.
ἐὰν δῶτε περὶ ἁμαρτίας, ἡ ψυχὴ ὑμῶν ὄψεται σπέρμα μακρόβιον.
καὶ κύριος βούλεται ἀφελεῖν ἀπὸ τοῦ πόνου τῆς ψυχῆς αὐτοῦ, δεῖξαι αὐτῷ φῶς καὶ πλάσαι τῇ συνέσει, δικαιῶσαι δίκαιον εὖ δουλεύοντα πολλοῖς. καὶ τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν αὐτὸς ἀνοίσει.
διὰ τοῦτο αὐτὸς κληρονομήσει πολλοὺς καὶ τῶν ἰσχυρῶν μεριεῖ σκῦλα: ἀνθ̓ ὧν παρεδόθη εἰς θάνατον ἡ ψυχὴ αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐν τοῖς ἀνόμοις ἐλογίσθη.
καὶ αὐτὸς ἁμαρτίας πολλῶν ἀνήνεγκεν καὶ διὰ τὰς ἁμαρτίας αὐτῶν παρεδόθη.
καὶ πάλιν αὐτός φησιν: Ἐγὼ δέ εἰμι σκώληξ καὶ οὐκ ἄνθρωπος, ὄνειδος ἀνθρώπων καὶ ἐξουθένημα λαοῦ.
πάντες οἱ θεωροῦντές με ἐξεμυκτήρισάν με, ἐλάλησαν ἐν χείλεσιν, ἐκίνησαν κεφαλήν: Ἤλπισεν ἐπὶ κύριον, ῥυσάσθω αὐτόν, σωσάτω αὐτόν, ὅτι θέλει αὐτόν.
ὁρᾶτε, ἅνδρες ἀγαπητοί, τίς ὁ ὑπογραμμὸς ὁ δεδομένος ἡμῖν: εἰ γὰρ ὁ κύριος οὕτως ἐταπεινοφρόνησεν, τί ποιήσωμεν ἡμεῖς οἱ ὑπὸ τὸν ζυγὸν τῆς χάριτος αὐτοῦ δἰ αὐτοῦ ἐλθόντες;
thought_title: The humble Christ as our pattern
orientation: The author presents Christ as the example of humility against the envy and faction in Corinth, quoting what the Holy Spirit said about him.
pass_a_gloss: For Christ is of those having humility, not of those exalting themselves over his flock. The sceptre of the greatness of God, the Lord Jesus Christ, did not come in boasting of arrogance nor of haughtiness, although being able, but having humility, just as the holy Spirit spoke concerning him: for it says: Lord, who believed our report? and to whom was the arm of the Lord revealed? We reported before him, as a child, as a root in thirsty ground: there is no form to him nor glory, and we saw him, and he had no form nor beauty, but his form was without honor, failing beside the form of men: a man being in a blow and in toil and knowing to bear sickness, because his face has been turned away, he was dishonored and was not counted. This one bears our sins and suffers pain for us, and we considered him to be in toil and in a blow and in affliction. But he was wounded because of our sins and has been made weak because of our acts of lawlessness. Discipline of our peace is upon him: by his bruise we were healed. We all as sheep were led astray, each man was led astray by his own way. And the Lord handed him over for our sins, and he, because of being afflicted, does not open his mouth. As a sheep was led to slaughter, and as a lamb voiceless before the one shearing it, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who will tell his generation? Because his life is taken away from the earth. From the acts of lawlessness of my people he comes to death. And I will give the wicked in return for his burial and the rich in return for his death: because he did no act of lawlessness, nor was deceit found in his mouth. And the Lord wishes to cleanse him from the blow. If you give for sin, your soul will see seed living a long time. And the Lord wishes to take away from the toil of his soul, to show him light and to form with understanding, to justify a righteous one serving well for many. And their sins he will bear up. Because of this he will inherit many and will divide spoils of the strong: in return for which his soul was handed over to death, and he was counted among the lawless. And he bore up sins of many and was handed over because of their sins. And again he says: But I am a worm and not a man, a reproach of men and a contempt of people. All those looking at me mocked me, they spoke with lips, they shook head: He hoped upon the Lord, let him rescue him, let him save him, because he wants him. You see, beloved men, what is the pattern given to us: for if the Lord so had humility, what should we do, we who have come under the yoke of his grace through him?

choices.why: Keeps brief glossary English humility for the ταπεινοφρον root instead of lowly minded.

choices.term: τὸ σκῆπτρον τῆς μεγαλωσύνης τοῦ θεοῦ
choices.english: the sceptre of the greatness of God
choices.why: Keeps the stark title as written, with Christ identified as the sceptre, rather than smoothing to power or majesty.
Renders the concrete state in the quotation, distinct from the moral having humility above.
Keeps a written example to be traced, fitting the closing appeal to what was given to us.

pass_b_english: Christ belongs to those who have humility, not to those who exalt themselves over his flock. The sceptre of the greatness of God, the Lord Jesus Christ, did not come with boastful arrogance or pride, though he could have done so. He came having humility, just as the Holy Spirit spoke about him. For this is what the Spirit says.

"Lord, who has believed our report, and to whom has the arm of the Lord been revealed? We proclaimed before him as a child, as a root in thirsty ground. He has no form or glory, and we saw him, and he had no form or beauty. His form was dishonored, fading beside the form of men. He was a man under blows and toil, knowing how to bear weakness, for his face was turned away. He was dishonored and not esteemed. He bears our sins and suffers for us, yet we thought he was under toil and blows and affliction. But he was wounded for our sins and weakened for our lawless deeds. The discipline of our peace is upon him, and by his bruise we were healed. We all went astray like sheep, each one straying on his own way, and the Lord handed him over for our sins. Because he was afflicted, he does not open his mouth. He was led like a sheep to slaughter, and like a lamb silent before its shearer, so he does not open his mouth. In his humiliation his judgment was taken away. Who will tell of his generation? For his life is taken from the earth. He goes to death for the lawless deeds of my people. And I will give the wicked for his burial and the rich for his death, for he did no lawlessness, and no deceit was found in his mouth. The Lord desires to cleanse him from the blow. If you make an offering for sin, your soul will see long-lived offspring. The Lord desires to lift the toil from his soul, to show him light and to shape him with understanding, to justify a righteous one who serves many well, and he himself will bear their sins. Therefore he will inherit many and will divide spoil with the strong, because his soul was handed over to death and he was counted among the lawless. He bore the sins of many and was handed over for their sins." (Isaiah 53:1-12)

"And again he himself says: 'But I am a worm and not a man, a reproach of men and contempt of the people. All who saw me mocked me, spoke with their lips, and shook their heads. He trusted in the Lord, let him rescue him, let him save him, since he delights in him.'" (Psalm 22:6-8)
See, dear friends, what pattern was given to us. If the Lord had humility in this way, what are we to do, we who have come through him under the yoke of his grace?

last_rejected.quote: will divide spoil with the strong
last_rejected.why: The genitive means he divides the spoils of the strong, not spoil shared with them.
last_rejected.fix: Therefore he will inherit many and will divide the spoils of the strong,
last_rejected.ruling: μεριεῖ σκῦλα with τῶν ἰσχυρῶν: LXX Isa 53:12 genitive after μερίζω can be 'divide the spoils of the strong' or 'share with'; 'with the strong' is a defensible rendering, not a clear error.
